tb21_profile.skill: Implement a distributed training schedule from a written spec: partition a transformer's layers across ranks, hand-roll forward/backward with P2P send/recv, and match a reference model's activations and gradients exactly
tb21_profile.domain: PyTorch, torch.distributed P2POp/rank/world_size, HuggingFace LlamaForCausalLM internals, autograd, tensor shape/dtype/device discipline
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec to a fixed function signature, verified numerically against a reference implementation; hard, many steps

searches: tools.py search rts "in parallel|worker processes|concurrenc|multiprocessing|thread pool|producer-consumer|pipeline stage" -n 25
tools.py search rebench "^" (repo histogram, grep for torch/keras/jax/transformers)

TMax-15K.reason: Split rows of a matrix across mpi4py ranks, gather, and keep log-softmax numerics exact — same distribute/communicate/verify loop.
Results must stop depending on the number of MPI processes; the TB test likewise demands identical output at world_size 1 and 2.
Write an MPI script where each rank owns a slice of the sweep, steps a stencil, and the ranks' results are reassembled exactly.
Reconstruct an nn.Module from state_dict keys/shapes and reproduce exact float outputs; same torch module-internals fluency.
Implement a parallel 2D integrator with mpi4py from a precise numerical spec and show convergence against reference values.
Fix a PyTorch model definition so the state_dict loads, then run eval-mode forward passes; layer-shape reasoning transfers.
Output ordering currently depends on which MPI rank finishes first; must impose deterministic cross-rank assembly.
Write an MPI parallel generator and prove its output matches a serial reference dataset — the same equivalence check.
Partition an integration range across MPI ranks and reduce partial results; basic rank arithmetic plus collective.
Rebuild lost inference code from weights and vocabulary; torch forward-pass reconstruction but no parallelism at all.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Build a PyTorch model from a JSON architecture spec and profile it per layer; module construction and per-layer accounting.
Configure a four-stage sequential pipeline executed by parallel workers; the toy shape of stage-wise pipelined execution.
Same staged-pipeline-with-N-workers construction; teaches stage ordering plus result collection, nothing about gradients.
Third variant of the parallel staged pipeline; only the worker-count configuration differs.
Write MPI source from scratch so every process prints its own rank out of the world size; rank/size API from a spec.
Fix MPI code so each process reports 'rank of size'; minimal multi-rank program correctness.
Repair an MPI hello-world so it emits rank and size and passes a process-level test.
Compile and launch a multi-process job under mpirun, fixing the runtime environment; launcher mechanics only.
Same mpirun launch/configuration chore; no algorithm and no inter-rank data movement.
Makefile targets to build and run an MPI hello-world; build automation, essentially no transfer.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Install CPU PyTorch and run a distributed training job on the gloo backend — the exact runtime this task initialises a process group in.
Define a nested nn.Module from a written architecture spec, run a forward pass, and report per-layer parameter/compute stats.
Same ezpz distributed training job launched under mpirun; torch distributed launch and rank environment variables.
Run an mpi4py program across two hosts, which forces correct rank/world configuration and inter-process communication.
Run the same workload at 1,2,4..12-way parallelism and check each run succeeds; mirrors the world_size sweep in the tests.
Build and run an MPI program that prints rank, world size and host; smallest possible multi-rank exercise.
Write a multiprocessing script that computes results in parallel and collects them; work splitting without communication.
Build and run three parallel-computing benchmarks; exposure to parallel decomposition of numeric workloads.
Launch an MPI benchmark through a container backend; multi-rank job orchestration, no algorithm work.
Build an MD simulator with MPI compilers and run it; mostly build plumbing in the HPC ecosystem.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Handling a custom torch.autograd.Function inside the traced computation graph; forward/backward graph reasoning is the crux here too.
Detect which submodules were never called during a forward — the TB tests likewise check each rank actually ran its layers.
Per-submodule parameter counting over a module tree; the same traversal you need to partition layers in a balanced way.
Correctly accumulating running mean/variance across many batches; same accumulate-over-microbatches numerics discipline.
Per-op flop accounting from a jit trace of a torch model; op-level understanding of a transformer's matmuls.
Flop counting for an einsum-based torch model; tensor-shape and op-semantics reasoning.
FlopCountAnalysis on a model with an unrecognised custom op; extending analysis over a torch module graph.
Checkpoint loading order breaks state_dict restore; relevant to moving a model's parameters between stages.
Rechunking arrays across dimensions: choosing a balanced partition of a big tensor is the same decision as layer partitioning.
HighLevelGraph leaking into scheduler optimisation; task-graph scheduling, the distant cousin of a pipeline schedule.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Changing the replica count changes fit/evaluate output — exactly the world_size-invariance bug class this task must avoid.
Batch-dimension indexing of torch tensors breaks for b x n x d inputs; the shape discipline the hidden-state plumbing needs.
MessagePassing codegen assumes an argument exists; reasoning about generated forward signatures in a torch module.
Autocasting silently converts int inputs to float; the same dtype-discipline trap as moving ids and hidden states to a dtype.
TorchScript model works in memory but type-mismatches after a save/load round trip; torch module serialization semantics.
A rank-1 tensor reaches code expecting a matrix; debugging shape contracts through a torch numerical stack.
Composing torch Linear/ReLU/Dropout layers into a callable module goes wrong; basic nn module composition.
Make LM batch construction reproducible with an explicit generator; reproducibility of a training step, in the HF stack.
Torch model breaks on a degenerate input partition (zero-degree nodes); edge cases of a partitioned input.
Seeding a data collator for pretraining reproducibility; same library, almost no overlapping capability.

final_top10.reason: Distribute rows of a matrix over mpi4py ranks and gather exact log-softmax results; closest thing in the pool to rank-partitioned exact compute.
Make numerical output independent of MPI process count, mirroring the world_size 1 vs 2 equivalence the verifier enforces.
Per-rank ownership of a slice of work in an MPI solver written to a precise spec, with results reassembled exactly.
Runs a torch distributed training job on the gloo CPU backend — the same process-group runtime this task builds on.
Custom autograd Function nodes inside the computation graph; forward/backward graph semantics are the crux of AFAB too.
Reconstruct an nn.Module from state_dict shapes and reproduce exact float outputs under eval; torch module internals.
Replica count changing model output is precisely the failure mode a pipeline-parallel implementation must not have.
Build a nested nn.Module from a written spec, run a forward pass, and account for parameters and compute per layer.
Walk a torch module tree counting parameters per submodule — the same traversal used to partition layers evenly.
Implement a parallel numerical kernel with mpi4py from a written spec and validate against reference convergence values.

notes: Nothing in the 56k pool mentions torch.distributed, pipeline/tensor parallelism, P2POp, all_reduce or world_size (verified by search); the corpus has no distributed-deep-learning tasks at all. I therefore split transfer into two halves: MPI rank-partitioning tasks (TMax has a genuinely useful cluster of ~30) for the split-work/communicate/match-reference skill, and PyTorch module-internals tasks (fvcore in SWE-Smith, torchmeter in TW/RTS, pyg/keras in Rebench) for the domain. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is the weakest corpus by far: its only distributed content is ~60 near-identical MPI hello-world compile chores, so ranks 5-10 there are low-confidence filler and should be discounted at merge. The original shortlists were near-useless here (generic 'ML data pipeline' and '/app file chore' lexical matches); >80% of what I kept came from my own searches.
